Ototoxicity: Chemotherapy drugs induce reactive oxygen species, leading to oxidative stress that damages cochlear hair cells, causing ototoxicity. This oxidative damage disrupts ion homeostasis and triggers apoptosis in these cells, impairing hearing and balance function.
Cardiotoxicity: Chemotherapy drugs induce reactive oxygen species, leading to oxidative stress and DNA damage, which triggers apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction. This disrupts cardiac cell energy production and structural integrity, impairing heart function and causing cardiotoxicity.
Peripheral Neuropathy: Chemotherapy drugs often induce reactive oxygen species, leading to oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in peripheral neurons, which damages axonal integrity and disrupts nerve signaling, causing peripheral neuropathy.
Mucositis: Chemotherapy agents induce reactive oxygen species, leading to oxidative stress and DNA damage, which disrupts cell proliferation and triggers apoptosis in rapidly dividing mucosal cells, resulting in tissue injury and inflammation characteristic of mucositis.
Hepatotoxicity: Chemotherapy drugs often induce hepatotoxicity by generating reactive oxygen species during metabolism, leading to oxidative stress and DNA damage in liver cells. This triggers apoptosis or necrosis through mitochondrial dysfunction and activation of cell death pathways, ultimately causing tissue injury.
Neutropenia: Chemotherapy drugs induce DNA damage and generate reactive oxygen species, leading to apoptosis and impaired proliferation of hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow, which results in decreased neutrophil production and neutrophil deficiency.
Thrombocytopenia: Chemotherapy drugs induce DNA damage and reactive oxygen species production in hematopoietic cells, leading to apoptosis in bone marrow megakaryocytes, which reduces platelet production. This cellular injury disrupts thrombopoiesis, resulting in thrombocytopenia.
Myelosuppression: Chemotherapy drugs induce DNA damage and generate reactive oxygen species, disrupting cellular replication and repair processes in rapidly dividing bone marrow cells. This leads to apoptosis and reduced hematopoietic stem cell function, impairing blood cell production and causing myelosuppression.
Nephrotoxicity: Chemotherapy drugs induce oxidative stress by generating reactive oxygen species, which damage cellular components and disrupt mitochondrial function, leading to apoptosis or necrosis in renal tubular cells. Additionally, they may cause direct DNA damage or activate receptor-mediated pathways that trigger calcium influx and cellular injury, ultimately impairing kidney function.
Hypersensitivity: Chemotherapy drugs induce reactive oxygen species, causing oxidative stress and cellular damage, which leads to DNA strand breaks and mitochondrial dysfunction, resulting in cell death and tissue injury. This triggers an immune response, causing hypersensitivity through inflammation and organ dysfunction.
